title: Which lock, and when a deadlock can happen

questions.stem: Per this page, what happens when one thread runs a class's `static synchronized` method while another thread runs a `synchronized` instance method of the same class?

options.text: They can run at the same time, since each takes a different lock
options.says: The page says the static method locks the Class object and the instance method locks this, so they can run concurrently.

options.text: They take turns, since both take the lock of the Class object
options.says: The page says only the static method locks the Class object; the instance method locks this.

options.text: The call fails, since a class may not mix these two kinds of lock
options.says: The page shows both methods in one class and says they simply use different locks.

questions.stem: Per this page, which set of conditions must all be present for a deadlock?

options.text: Mutual exclusion, hold and wait, lock timeouts and random backoff
options.says: The page names lock timeouts and randomized backoff as ways to avoid or break deadlock and livelock, not as deadlock conditions.

options.text: Mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption and circular wait
options.says: The page lists exactly these four as the conditions a deadlock requires.

options.text: Unfair locks, long lock holds, thread priorities and busy waiting
options.says: The page names unfair locks, long lock holds and priorities as causes of starvation, not as deadlock conditions.
